rows.title: Client feedback myths vs facts: 3-business-day review window, deemed approval vs choice (approve/new date/cut scope), one approver + backup, one combined notes list
rows.caption:
Day 9 and still no feedback? That's not a client problem. It's a missing clause.

3 myths that keep you waiting:
1. "Waiting is part of the job." Fact: put a review window in the SOW.
2. "Silence means yes." Fact: only if your contract says so. Otherwise they choose: approve, a new date, or cut scope.
3. "More reviewers, better work." Fact: one named approver + a backup, one combined list of notes per round.

The clause (example terms, not legal advice):
- Review window: 3 business days per round
- One named approver + a backup
- One combined list of notes per round
- Late notes move the delivery date

Save this for your next SOW. Send it to the friend still waiting on feedback.

rows.title: First-frame tier list: S result on screen + 1 line, A face mid-sentence + text, B plain text, C silent b-roll, F logo intro
rows.caption:
Your first frame does more work than your hook line. Ranked, S to F:

S: the result on screen + one line of text (payoff first)
A: your face mid-sentence + text
B: text on a plain background
C: slow b-roll with no text
F: a logo intro or a black frame

Quick test: pause on frame one with the sound off. If it makes sense alone, it's working.

Send this to the friend whose reels open on a logo. Save it for your next edit.

rows.title: Sticky notes to client pitch deck with Claude Whiteboards (beta): dump, group by theme, turn board into a deck (Byte fixes EP 10)
rows.caption:
12 hours to a client pitch. 0 slides. 20 sticky notes. (Byte fixes · EP 10)

Claude Whiteboards (beta, on paid plans, web/desktop/mobile) can turn a board into a doc or a presentation:
1. Paste every sticky note onto one board
2. Ask Claude to group them by theme (problem, plan, price)
3. Ask it to turn the board into a deck, then rewrite it in your own words

The draft is a start. You own the pitch.
